findings.reason: a done-when that cites a command no longer registered cannot be reproduced as written, and the plan is a live record whose citations must resolve against the code it governs.
findings.text: §6's done-when names the command `reckon crew review-plan --dry-run`, but no such verb resolves: `reckon crew --help` lists only `review` (output line `review  Review one plan's content, …`), the sole registration is `@crew.command(name="review")` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2104`), and the surface emits `reckon crew review --project …` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:177`); the retired spelling also appears at lines 97, 229, 250 and 330 — §34 itself correctly uses `reckon crew review --plan <slug>`

response_events.reason: the finding is on landed s6, whose text records the verb as it was named when it shipped; the current verb is reckon crew review, which s34 and the review surface use, and a landed section is not rewritten for a later rename

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §34's own citations all resolve (see below), but an out-of-scope section cites a retired CLI verb.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §34's done-when names a measurable test (two content reviews in a temp crew home; the second after the first is promoted reads attempt 1, kind `dispatch`), a second case that ordinary implementation nodes still read `redispatch` at attempt 2, and a declared negative control (dispatch the review as before → attempt 2, kind `redispatch`, test fails). The ordinary-node clause is consistent with `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1436-1478`, where `attempt` climbs only for non-empty `prior_node_runs`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §34 puts its negative-control log under the run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`), a durable path, and names no session scratchpad or node-local temporary for evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §34 introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into code or comments; the new test file `tests/test_a_new_plan_review_is_a_first_attempt.py` is named by behaviour, and `PLAN_REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX = "plan-review-of-"` is a node-id prefix, not a plan label.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. (1) The stated root cause matches the cited evidence: sampling `attempt.json` in the 2026-10-16 run directories shows `a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline` at attempts 24-36 and `the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches` at 44-49, each a fresh `r-<stamp>-plan-review-of-…` run with kind `redispatch` and a lineage (e.g. `r-20261016T165041841408` records `attempt` 36, `attempt_kind` `redispatch`), exactly the climbing-attempt symptom §34 names. (2) The mechanism produces the done-when: `dispatch()` reads its attempt/kind from `prior_node_runs` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1436-1478`), and the queued request record persists `dispatch_options` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:226-265`) which `_launch_queued` replays (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:159-197`), so a first-attempt marker carried in those options reaches `dispatch()` on both routes §34 names. (3) The mechanism runs on the real code path with its callers named: `_dispatch_composed_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1774`) calls `dispatch_module.dispatch(... dispatch_options=...)` directly, and the held route relaunches through `_launch_queued`; the two readers §34 names for the misreading exist — `reckon/calibration.py:122-126` discards durations from `attempt > 1`, and `attempts` is a field of the picker request (`reckon/crew/picker/types.py:17`, consumed at `reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py:430`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 carries one deliverable (a plan review is dispatched as a first attempt), with the exclusion of `crew redispatch`'s lane-change recorded as a boundary rather than a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §34 declares no depends-on or gates and needs none; its two named callers of `dispatch()` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:_launch_queued`) both resolve, and the plan's `informs` edges on the meta are unchanged by this section.
